an4.95:1.1: “Monks, these four types of individuals are to be found existing in the world.
an4.95:1.3: The one who practices neither for his/her own benefit nor for that of others.
an4.95:1.4: The one who practices for the benefit of others but not for his/her own.
an4.95:1.5: The one who practices for his/her own benefit but not for that of others.
an4.95:1.6: The one who practices for his/her own benefit and for that of others.“
an4.95:2.1: Just as a firebrand from a funeral pyre—burning at both ends, covered with excrement in the middle—is used as fuel neither in a village nor in the wilderness:
an4.95:2.2: I tell you that this is a simile for the individual who practices neither for his/her own benefit nor for that of others.
an4.95:3.1: The individual who practices for the benefit of others but not for his/her own is the higher & more refined of these two.
an4.95:3.2: The individual who practices for his/her own benefit but not for that of others is the highest & most refined of these three.
an4.95:3.3: The individual who practices for his/her own benefit and for that of others is, of these four, the foremost, the chief, the most outstanding, the highest, & supreme.
an4.95:4.1: Just as from a cow comes milk; from milk, curds; from curds, butter; from butter, ghee; from ghee, the skimmings of ghee; and of these, the skimmings of ghee are reckoned the foremost—
an4.95:4.2: in the same way, of these four, the individual who practices for his/her own benefit and for that of others is the foremost, the chief, the most outstanding, the highest, & supreme.
an4.95:4.3: “These are the four types of individuals to be found existing in the world.”
